rationale: The Court is likely to affirm unanimously on a narrow Watson-centered ground: WWII-era contracting and wartime regulation do not show defendants were “acting under” a federal officer with respect to the Louisiana-permitted dredging/restoration conduct the complaints target, and the “or relating to” amendment cannot supply a limiting principle by itself. A concurrence is most likely from a textualist (Thomas/Gorsuch) to emphasize the independent force of “acting under” and to cabin expansive readings of § 1442 that would federalize ordinary state land-and-resource disputes.
